headline: Job postings for US software developers have risen by nearly 15% since February 2025 even as AI takes over more of the coding.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: hard figures from Indeed Hiring Lab, Stanford and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, but read through a relay because CNBC's own page was blocked.
importance_line: What changed is that developer demand is recovering despite AI coding tools, which matters first to working developers and new graduates, since the gains go mostly to senior and AI-related roles, then to employers and universities, but postings are not hires and are still far below the pre-pandemic level.
summary: CNBC reports, in an account relayed by UA.NEWS, that US software developer job postings are up nearly 15% since February 2025, when Anthropic launched its Claude Code coding tool, but remain about 27.5% below their pre-pandemic level, according to Indeed Hiring Lab, the research arm of the Indeed job site. Senior roles made up 71% of the growth between May 2025 and May 2026, while Stanford's 2026 AI Index shows employment of early-career developers down 20%.
notes: CNBC page returned 403. Text read from UA.NEWS's account of the CNBC story (https://ua.news/en/it-ta-telekom/vakansiyi-dlia-rozrobnikiv-u-ssha-zrosli-maizhe-na-15-popri-shi-cnbc); link kept on CNBC as the original. Figures are as relayed, not checked against Indeed, Stanford or the BLS.
